archetype.name: Gunslinger
archetype.definition: A veteran aggressive thrower who works the intermediate and deep levels and holds the ball to let routes develop, accepting interceptions and sacks as the cost of chunk plays, and this season is no different from his career.

report.headline: Same Winston as ever: deep shots land, short game and turnovers drag him under.
report.take:
Winston took over from Jaxson Dart and has started two games, after playing 88% of the snaps in the Week 2 loss at the Rams. Nothing in his profile is new. His time to throw (2.78s), aggressiveness (21.8% of throws into tight windows) and intended air yards (9.27) sit right on top of his Tampa and Cleveland numbers. This is the quarterback who threw for 5,109 yards and 30 interceptions in 2019. He hunts the throw downfield and lives with what comes back.

The season line ranks 37th of 42 in EPA per dropback, but it is lopsided. The Rams game, against a defense now ranked 4th, accounts for -16.5 of his passing EPA on roughly 29 dropbacks: 11 of 27 with a 29.6% bad-throw rate. Across the two starts against Tennessee and Arizona he has been close to break-even, and the Arizona game (250 yards, 3 TDs, +3.9 EPA) was the first time the full package showed up. The path runs from awful to bad to playable, and the opponents got softer along the way.

The splits flip the usual quarterback profile. On 12 deep throws he has +1.03 EPA per attempt and a +14.5 CPOE. On 35 short throws he is at -0.32 EPA with a -19.8 CPOE, and the 12 throws behind the line, mostly screens, have lost value despite an 83% completion rate. A veteran does not suddenly lose the ability to complete 5-yard passes. That short-game number is the most likely thing on his card to regress back toward normal. The deep number is also running hot on a dozen attempts. The interceptions are not a fluke: three on 19 intermediate throws, and a career-long pattern of ranking near the bottom in picks.

The context is not helping. The Giants pass 10 points less than expected in neutral situations, 30th in the league, so he is often throwing on long third downs (9.5 yards to go on average, 30% converted). The line ranks 30th in QB hit rate allowed, which feeds a 10.3% sack rate. His pressure-to-sack rate (31.3%) matches his career range, so the sacks are partly a holding-the-ball trait and partly the protection. Under center and off play action, the offense has worked: +0.23 EPA on 18 plays, against -0.33 from shotgun.

strengths.title: Still completes the deep ball
strengths.body: Twelve throws of 20+ air yards have produced +1.03 EPA per attempt and a 14.5-point CPOE, and he keeps taking those shots at his career rate. The sample is tiny and will cool off. Still, deep accuracy and willingness have been part of his game for a decade, so the shots remain a real source of offense rather than noise.

strengths.title: Play action from under center
strengths.body: On 18 under-center dropbacks he has a +0.23 EPA and a 50% success rate. That fits a run-leaning offense that sells the run and gives him clean intermediate windows. It is a small sample, but it points to the version of this offense that suits him.

strengths.title: Trending up as competition eases
strengths.body: His passing EPA went from -16.5 at the Rams to -6.1 against Tennessee to +3.9 against Arizona. Part of that is opponent quality, with the 4th-, 21st- and 27th-ranked defenses now. Part of it is him settling in as the starter after coming off the bench.

concerns.title: Interceptions are who he is
concerns.body: His 3.8% interception rate ranks 36th, and all three picks came on 19 intermediate throws. His career ranks in interceptions sit near the bottom almost every year, so this is the cost of his style, not bad luck. Expect roughly one pick a game to continue.

concerns.title: Short game has collapsed
concerns.body: A -19.8 CPOE on throws of 0-9 air yards, plus negative value on throws behind the line, has stalled the offense. The middle of the field is worse, at 41% completions with a -20.7 CPOE. His heaviest target, Isaiah Likely, is returning -0.25 EPA per target on 26 looks. Some of this should normalize toward his career CPOE, but until it does, drives depend on hitting a big play.

concerns.title: Sacks from line and style
concerns.body: A 10.3% sack rate ranks 38th, and 21.6% of his dropbacks end in a hit or sack. The line is 30th in hit rate allowed, and his 31.3% pressure-to-sack rate is consistent with a career of holding the ball. Neither part is likely to change, so drive-killing sacks stay in his profile.

trend.note: Three appearances, each better than the last: -16.5, -6.1, then +3.9 passing EPA. The best game came against the softest defense, so the rise is real but partly schedule-driven.

nextGame.headline: Washington's leaky deep defense meets the throws he actually completes.
nextGame.body:
Washington's defense matches his strengths and weaknesses closely. It ranks 5th against short passes, where he has been at his worst. Against deep passes it ranks 26th, allowing +1.08 EPA per attempt, which is where he has been at his best. Quarterbacks have scored 22.5 PPR points a game against Washington (30th) with three touchdowns a game (31st). The pass rush is middling, 23rd in sack rate, which matters for a quarterback who holds the ball behind a line that leaks.

Availability favors him on both sides. Safety Nick Cross, a 99%-snap starter, is out, and fellow starting safety Jeremy Reaves is questionable with a finger injury. That leaves Washington's back end thin against a passer who wants to throw over the top. Edge Charles Omenihu is questionable too. Washington's offense is battered: Jayden Daniels is listed out with a dislocated elbow, though Dan Quinn is aiming for him to start. Mariota is doubtful, and McLaurin, Cosmi and White are out. If Daniels sits, this becomes a lower-scoring, run-heavy game, which suits the Giants' approach. On the Giants' side, only depth receiver Braxton Berrios (9% of snaps) is on the report.

keyMatchups.title: His deep shots vs. thinned safeties
keyMatchups.body: Washington is 26th in deep-pass EPA allowed, and Cross, a 99%-snap starter, is out. Winston's best throws have been 20+ yards downfield. Expect two or three shots, any of which can swing the game.

keyMatchups.title: Short passing into a tough unit
keyMatchups.body: Washington's 5th-ranked short-pass defense meets his worst area, with a -0.32 EPA on short throws. Underneath completions likely won't sustain drives, so third-and-long and sacks remain a threat.

keyMatchups.title: Washington's quarterback situation
keyMatchups.body: Daniels is listed out and Mariota is doubtful. Washington's offense was already 29th in success rate. A limited Daniels or a backup would keep the game script neutral, letting the Giants stay run-first and protect Winston from obvious passing downs.

nextGame.watch: Whether the early downfield shots connect against Washington's depleted secondary. If they do, he can produce his best line of the season. If not, he gets stuck in third-and-long against a defense that takes away the short game.

restOfSeason.body:
The style is fixed: aggressive throws, roughly 2.8 seconds to throw, a high bad-throw rate, about one interception a game and plenty of sacks behind a line that ranks 30th in hits allowed. What should improve is the short game. A -19.8 CPOE underneath is far outside anything in his career, and normal short accuracy would lift his efficiency from bottom-five toward the low-average range he has posted across his starts. The deep efficiency (+1.03 EPA on 12 throws) and his red-zone touchdowns will cool, so a fair baseline is his last two starts, about break-even per dropback, rather than the season line or the Arizona game.

Volume will cap him. The Giants pass far less than situations predict, so expect around 180-240 yards in most weeks, with spikes against weak secondaries. Whether he keeps the job matters as much as how he plays. He is listed QB1, but Dart started the first two weeks, and a turnover-heavy stretch could reopen the question.
swingFactors: Whether his short-throw accuracy returns to his career norm
Holding the QB1 job over Jaxson Dart
Pass protection, 30th in hit rate allowed

bets.reason: Washington allows three passing TDs a game to quarterbacks (31st) and ranks 26th against deep passes, and starting safety Cross is out. Deep throws and red-zone throws are where his touchdowns have come from.

His average includes a game off the bench against the 4th-ranked defense. Washington allows 270.8 passing yards a game (23rd) and leaks deep plays. The run-heavy Giants game plan keeps this a lean rather than a like.

He has a 3.8% INT rate, three picks on 19 intermediate throws, a 15.4% bad-throw rate and a career of bottom-tier interception totals. Washington's tight short coverage pushes him toward the riskier throws.

Washington's offense is 29th in success rate, and its quarterback, top receiver and right guard are all on the report. The Giants have covered both of Winston's starts. The edge shrinks if Daniels plays at full strength.

confidence.note: 78 attempts over three games, one in relief; deep and short splits rest on small samples; Washington's QB status unsettled.
